> [!IMPORTANT]
> **This is a stopgap fix.** It is meant to unblock users until the real `ClientStateVar` refactor lands. The refactor will handle this case much more cleanly and **without creating extra React states** in components that only set the value. Treat this change as temporary: the refactor should replace it rather than build on it.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

### Description

Users reported frontend errors when sibling components share a global `rx._x.client_state` var (`global_ref=True`): one sibling renders `.value` and another sets it from a user interaction.

**Root cause:** `ClientStateVar.set` / `set_value()` returned a Var that referenced `refs['_client_state_set<name>']` but didn't carry the `useState`/`useId`/`refs` hooks that define it. Auto-memoization compiles the setter-only sibling into its own memo body, so the setter only worked if a component rendering `.value` had already mounted and defined the function. When no reader was mounted (for example, the reader sits behind an `rx.cond`), the setter threw:

```
TypeError: refs._client_state_set<name> is not a function
```

**Fix:**
- For global vars (`global_ref=True`), the setter Var now carries the `ClientStateVar`'s `VarData`. Every component that sets the value registers its own `useState` instance in the shared `refs` setter dict, and the global setter fans out to all of them.
- `create()` now keeps the default's full `VarData`, so a backend-derived default (`default=State.field`) brings its state `useContext` hook along.
- Local vars (`global_ref=False`) are unchanged. A setter-only sibling still fails loudly with `setX is not defined`, instead of silently updating a private copy of the state that no reader sees.

**Trade-offs of this stopgap (all addressed by the upcoming refactor):**
- Components that only set the value now hold an extra `useState` and re-render when the value changes.
- The setter's `useCallback` now lists the client-state hook values as dependencies, so it is recreated on every value change.
- With a backend-derived default (`default=State.field`), a setter-only component now also subscribes to that whole backend state through `useContext`. It re-renders, and recreates its `onClick`, on every delta to any field of that state, even though `useState` only reads the default on mount.
- Setter-only components also add an entry to `refs['_client_state_dict_set<name>']` that is never removed on unmount, as readers already did before this PR. Every set call still invokes the setters of unmounted components.

### Follow-ups for the `ClientStateVar` refactor

These are out of scope for this stopgap:
- Don't give setter-only components their own React state.
- Don't subscribe setter-only components to the default's backend state after mount.
- Remove per-instance entries from the setter and value dicts on unmount (e.g. `useEffect` cleanup).
- Allow backend `push()` / `retrieve()` to work when no component using the var is mounted. Today `run_script` can't carry hooks, so both require a mounted component. This is unchanged by this PR.
- Local (`global_ref=False`) vars still can't be shared between components that auto-memoize separately. This is inherent to local state and unchanged by this PR.

### Tests

- `tests/units/experimental/test_client_state.py` (new):
  - Global setters carry the client state hooks, for both `.set` and `.set_value(...)`.
  - Local setters don't carry them.
  - A backend-derived default's hooks reach `.value`, `.set` and `.set_value(...)`.
- `tests/units/compiler/test_memoize_plugin.py`: the memo for a setter-only sibling contains `useState` and defines the `refs` setter.
- `tests/integration/tests_playwright/test_client_state.py` (new): browser tests for three cases:
  - siblings that are both mounted
  - a setter clicked before its reader mounts behind an `rx.cond`
  - a backend-derived default with a sibling setter

The unit tests, the cond-reader browser test and the backend-default browser test fail without their fixes and pass with them. The both-mounted browser test also passed before the fix and is kept as a guard. The full unit suite passes, and ruff and pyright are clean.
